subject: Next steps: Novalytics trial resourcing & success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novalytics.com>, platform@novalytics.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Next steps: Novalytics trial resourcing & success criteria

Hi Elena / Novalytics team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth before we lock dates:

1) High-level goal
- Run a 2-week evaluation of Redwood Inference integrated with Novalytics' ranking pipeline to validate cost/latency at production-like load and confirm model quality against your golden prompts.

2) Success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for 512-token requests at 8 RPS sustained per model shard.
- Throughput: support 8 concurrent RPS with headroom to burst to 18 RPS for short periods.
- Quality: no >5% regression on your top-10 relevance metric when comparing current baseline -> Redwood-optimized model.
- Stability: <1% error rate (server errors / OOMs) over a 48-hour steady-state window.

3) Trial timing & ownership
- Proposed trial window: Mon Jan 24 — Sun Feb 6 (2 weeks). Please confirm if that works.
- Redwood leads: Ben Carter (sales, trial coordinator), Dev Patel (engineer, trial runbook & infra).
- Novalytics leads: Elena Rossi (POC owner), Marco Gallo (platform contact).

4) Capacity and autoscaling (initial proposal)
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) for sustained load.
- Burst policy: allow up to +2 GPUs (total 4) for short periods (auto-burst) with fast warmup.
- Autoscale triggers: add a GPU when avg GPU utilization > 70% for 90s OR queue latency > 120ms for 60s; remove when utilization < 45% for 3 minutes and queue empty.
- Model variant: redwood-medium-quantized (good balance of cost & latency); we can test a smaller quantized variant if quality holds.
- Warm caches: we recommend a KV prefix cache warmed in the first 30 minutes of the test window to avoid cold-start penalties.

5) Deliverables before kickoff
- Signed trial order (attachment): redwood-trial-template.pdf (attached).
- SOC2 and data handling confirmation (send any vendor forms you need).
- Shared eval prompt set (you mentioned a 200-case set) and a dedicated S3 bucket for logs/outputs.

6) Next steps (action items)
- Elena: confirm trial start date and owner for the eval prompt set by EOD Fri Jan 13.
- Novalytics: return the signed trial order or request edits by Jan 17.
- Redwood (Dev): prepare capacity runbook and estimate of incremental cost for burst GPUs by Jan 12.
- Redwood (Ben): schedule kickoff for week of Jan 24.

Attachments: redwood-trial-template.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — look forward to getting this spinning.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Gallo <marco.gallo@novalytics.com>, platform@novalytics.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Next steps: Novalytics trial resourcing & success criteria

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side before we sign off:

- Trial window: Jan 24 works in principle but we need a short internal alignment on the evaluation rubric. Can you give us until Jan 18 to confirm?
- Success criteria: the team is particularly sensitive to tokenized latency for longer requests. Can we add p95 for up to 2,000 tokens as a secondary metric? If that is likely to be >1s we want to understand tradeoffs.
- Capacity: overnight workloads peak lower; to save cost we'd prefer baseline 1 reserved GPU with autoscale to 3. Is that feasible without impacting p95 targets? If not, propose the minimum baseline that keeps steady-state p95 stable.
- Security/data: we will need BYOK for keys and a short note on retention of logs (we prefer logs deleted after 90 days unless retained for debugging by mutual consent). Also please attach SOC2 artifact or your SOC2 report link.

I've attached an evaluation metrics sheet that includes our top-20 prompts and a rough traffic pattern (weekday spikes).

Attachment: novalytics-eval-metrics.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If you can respond to capacity/BYOK/SOC2 questions this week, we'll aim to return a signed trial order the following week.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Engineering | Novalytics, Inc.
elena.rossi@novalytics.com

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 08:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Next steps: Novalytics trial resourcing & success criteria

Elena — looping in technical context and a concrete capacity proposal from infra side. Replying to the points you raised:

1) BYOK / SOC2
- BYOK: supported via our KMS integrations; we can do a customer-managed key in AWS KMS for the trial environment. We'll provide a short HOWTO and a sample access policy.
- SOC2: attaching a redwood SOC2 summary link in the Drive (see related links). If you need the full report we can share under NDA; let us know.

2) Latency for long requests (2,000 tokens)
- Estimations: on redwood-medium-quantized we expect p95 ~ 700-900ms for 2k tokens under dedicated GPU with warmed KV cache. If you require <1s, we should maintain at least 2 reserved GPUs to avoid queueing during your daytime spikes.

3) Baseline vs burst (proposed concrete plan)
- Baseline: 1 reserved A100-equivalent GPU for nights + maintenance windows.
- Daytime policy: schedule a time-based autoscale increase to 2 reserved GPUs from 08:00-20:00 CET for weekdays; allow autoscale burst to 3 GPUs when queue latency > 120ms for >60s or GPU util > 75% for 90s.
- Burst cap: 3 GPUs total for the trial (we can expand temporarily but will surface estimated cost).
- Warmup and spin-up: cold GPU spin-up ~= 90-120s for a new instance; we will pre-warm model weights and KV cache when a scheduled scale event is expected.

4) Cost estimate (rough)
- Baseline 1 GPU (2 weeks): approx $5,200. Scheduled daytime extra GPU (weekdays): incremental $3,400. Burst budget (on-demand): set aside $1,200 as buffer for transient spikes. Total estimated incremental trial infra: ~$9.8k. We'll provide a formal cost sheet in the capacity runbook.

5) Runbook & attachments
- Attached: capacity-runbook.md (runbook excerpt) and a short checklist we'll follow for the 2-week run. Runbook includes autoscale knobs, escalation path, and rollback policy.

If that plan looks reasonable, we can proceed with baseline=1, scheduled weekday=+1, burst cap=3, and we will monitor p95 closely. Ben — if Novalytics signs, we'll schedule a 60-minute technical kickoff to finalize cache warming and on-call rotation.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachment: capacity-runbook.md (text/markdown)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps: Novalytics trial resourcing & success criteria

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the metrics sheet. Per Lauren's note above we've adjusted the plan to what we think balances cost and p95 targets:

- Trial dates: tentatively Jan 24 — Feb 6. We can shift if you need until Jan 31 start at latest.
- Capacity: baseline 1 reserved GPU, scheduled +1 GPU weekdays 08:00-20:00 CET, burst cap to 3 GPUs. Lauren's team will monitor p95 for 2k token requests and advise if we need to convert to 2 baseline GPUs.
- Security: Redwood supports BYOK; I'll share the HOWTO and the SOC2 NDA link today.
- Docs / signatures: please review and sign the trial order (DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Doc-123). If you prefer edits, mark up and we can route to legal.

Action items summary:
- Elena/Novalytics: confirm acceptance of the capacity plan and sign DocuSign by EOD Jan 20 to keep Jan 24 kickoff.
- Ben (me): circulate kickoff invite for week of Jan 24 once signed.
- Lauren/Dev: final runbook and cost sheet delivered by Jan 20.

I'll also set up a short 30-minute sync next week for technical clarifications if your engineers want to dig in before the kickoff.

Appreciate the collaboration — excited to get this live.
